LESSON: BEADING

Grade: PP1
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: ORNAMENTS
Topic 8.1: Beading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Beading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What materials do you leaner should be able to: collect locally available materials need for beading?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BEADING
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Beading helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BEADING
Study Beading like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work

What this means
In this part you learn to Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Beading” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Beading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Beading” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Beading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Beading from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Beading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Beading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What materials do you leaner should be able to: collect locally available materials need for beading?
2. What item can you • Learners to sort the materials to beading use make from beads?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Beading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Appreciate own and others • Observe safety as they bead finished beading work • Learners to express their emotions as they display their work.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
